description: Team Al-Biruni Geodesy is solving "Harmonization of MODIS & VIIRS Hot Spots". We use web dev, GIS mapping, and Python pipelines with NASA FIRMS data to build an open-source fire risk sentinel.
summary:
For the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge, Al-Biruni Geodesy developed an advanced, open-source web dashboard that reconciles millions of raw satellite detections from NASA’s MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) sensors into high-fidelity, verified wildfire events. Using a robust 1.5 km spatial-temporal chord fusion algorithm, our platform effectively cuts down data clutter and eliminates false alarms while locking in dual-sensor confirmed hotspots.

To empower emergency responders and researchers, the application features an interactive split-screen curtain comparison map and a location-aware AI Wildfire Spread Predictor that dynamically computes real-time threat indices, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) metrics, and carbon emission flux based on active regional clusters. Built using React, Vite, and a zero-key Leaflet engine, Al-Biruni Geodesy delivers accessible, high-precision orbital fire intelligence to communities worldwide without relying on proprietary barriers.
details:
• Al-Biruni Geodesy is an advanced orbital wildfire intelligence platform designed to reconcile millions of raw satellite detections from NASA’s MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) sensors into high-fidelity, verified wildfire events. The system utilizes a robust 1.5 km spatial-temporal chord fusion algorithm to filter out false alarms and background thermal noise, cross-confirming dual-sensor hotspots. It features an interactive split-screen curtain map ("Raw vs. Clean") and a location-aware AI Wildfire Spread Predictor that dynamically computes real-time threat indices, Fire Radiative Power (FRP), and carbon emission flux based on active regional clusters.
    image_799804.png
    • Clutter Reduction: Effectively eliminates background sensor anomalies, providing emergency responders with clean, actionable intelligence.
    • Real-Time Threat Assessment: Enables local authorities and researchers to evaluate wildfire risk and spread velocity instantly for any searched region or global hot-spot.
    • Intended Impact: To democratize access to high-precision Earth observation data, helping vulnerable communities and environmental agencies anticipate, monitor, and mitigate wildfire disasters more efficiently.
    • Frontend & Visualization: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet.js (zero-key map engine), GSAP (ScrollTrigger).
    • Data Processing & Analytics: Python (pandas, numpy, scipy.spatial.cKDTree) for spatial-temporal fusion of NASA FIRMS active fire archives and NRT datasets.
      image_799804.png
    • Deployment & Hosting: Vercel cloud infrastructure & GitHub version control (nasif120696-collab/al-biruni-geodesy-v1).
    • Zero Proprietary Barriers: Built completely open-source without requiring paid API keys, making it accessible to researchers and local teams anywhere in the world.
    • Split-Screen Curtain Interface: Offers a unique side-by-side comparative visualization allowing users to instantly contrast raw sensor clutter against cleaned, dual-sensor verified events.
    • Location-Aware AI Telemetry: Seamlessly links map searches and regional presets with live threat scoring and FRP analytics.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
